items.label: ASE Group Q1 FY2026 (04-29-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Raised 2026 LEAP (leading-edge advanced packaging) revenue guidance

set.signal: Raised 2026 LEAP (leading-edge advanced packaging) revenue guidance: CFO Joseph Tung now expects LEAP services revenue 'around 10% above our prior guidance, reaching over $3.5 billion' ('we are more than doubling our LEAP revenue this year'), with even stronger incremental revenue growth expected in 2027. Full-process LEAP lines are in tuning and qualification, with their revenue ramping mostly in Q4 2026 (LEAP ~75% assembly / 25% test; test ~75% wafer sort / 25% final test). CPO: developing with the foundry and the end customer; no number yet; ASE 'will start with the packaging part of it' (CPO test 'is more complicated than the regular chips that we are testing now'); 'once it gets into a volume scale, that we would definitely be a very critical partner'. Panel-level: a fully automated pilot line is installed for customer qualification, with small mass-production volume expected from 2027. Raising capex (machinery +USD 0.6B, mostly LEAP wafer sort, deployed in Q4 to support the 2027 capacity ramp); outside Taiwan the main investment is in Malaysia (a factory acquired from ADI, to serve as buffer capacity for demand from outside Taiwan) plus a test ramp in Singapore mostly for AI-related test. For now resources are focused on wafer sort rather than final test, as ASE is tight in both facility and capacity.
set.figure: LEAP 2026 over $3.5 billion (more than doubling YoY); panel small mass production from 2027

items.reason: 'incl. for a large GPU customer' came from the analyst's (Gokul Hariharan, JPMorgan) question about final test; the CFO answered only that the focus stays on wafer sort. The figure's 'CPO + panel-level ramping' contradicts the CFO (CPO 'still at a very early stage'; panel is a pilot line). Quotes now verbatim, speakers attributed. Verifier: CPO test wording made verbatim; figure keeps the call's '$3.5 billion'.
items.evidence: Yeah, I think the primarily, I think we will be focusing our resources in wafer sort at this point. I think we are tight in both facility as well as in capacity.
